packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, one packet per session, prompt and images only (reader brief of PR #76/#77); repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response; reread of packets whose first readings were written after the session's image limit had removed earlier images
text:
packet-06 -- blind first reading (unverified image reading)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this packet. Beyond the brief's rules I only listed the image filenames/pixel sizes in the packet directory (python glob + PIL) to know how many tiles there are.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview face 1)
- Small parchment fragment, roughly 7.5 cm wide x 6 cm high against the scale (approx. x 695-1205, y 430-855 in the overview). Stained, worn, with holes and a torn lower-left / left edge.
- Visible structure from left to right:
  (a) a narrow strip at the far left (x ~700-770) carrying line-ENDINGS of a column whose beginnings are lost (e.g. "...dem", "...ordine"-like endings visible in the lower half);
  (b) a largely blank/stained band (x ~770-860) -- intercolumnar space or margin; a vertical fold/strip join at about x 800 (the bottom label "Stams StA Frag. 34h"(?) sits here);
  (c) a column of line-BEGINNINGS (x ~860-950) whose right part runs into a vertical crease/cut at x ~950; near its foot a larger-script "Per xpm" (per Christum?) line beginning -- possibly a rubric/formula written in larger letters;
  (d) right of the crease a column (x ~955-1200) with c. 30 lines of small Gothic textualis/cursiva-influenced book hand; damage (abrasion, white loss) in its upper middle.
- Modern pencil shelfmark at foot: "Stams StA Frag. 34h"(?) under (b), and "IX a/N 29"(?) under (d) -- modern, not text.
- Whether (c) and (d) are one column split by a crease or two columns is not certain from the overview; tile reading should decide.
- No colour visible in the overview (photo is low-res); the larger "Per xpm" suggests a highlighted formula. No marginal/interlinear glosses seen at this scale.


TILE image-002.jpg (upper-left of face 1; native res). Shows: left strip of line-endings (x 60-300), blank/stained band with fold at x ~480-520 and a hole at x 540,y 655, column of line-beginnings (x 690-1085), vertical crease/cut at x ~1085-1095, then start of the right column (x 1095-1199, only first letters).
Interpretation: the left strip and the column at x 690 are separated by a wide blank band (c. 400 px) -- looks like a margin/gutter, so the left strip is probably the end of a column on the other leaf/side of a fold, i.e. this face may be an opening across a fold (tentative). The crease at x ~1090 runs straight down and the column at x 690 seems to continue past it into the right column (text at 1095+ aligns with the same lines), so (c)+(d) of the survey are probably ONE column with a crease through it (tentative).
Script: small Gothic cursive-influenced book hand (two-compartment-less a, looped ascenders on d/b/l, long s, heavy abbreviation), brown ink faded; very hard to read at this resolution. Crops: crops/packet-06/i002_col.jpg (column, autocontrast x2), i002_left.jpg (left strip).

Column of line-beginnings (x 690-1085) -- line numbers from top of image-002:
002.01  [..] ꝫ? multa? [illegible] ...        (first line at top edge, abraded)
002.02  eo? mihi? / cõmisi? [illegible] ...

002.04  obsc(ur)o? / absco? nḡe? [illegible]
002.05  ꝑdu? / ꝑdit? (p(er)...) [illegible]
002.06  Si illis bene? / Diu? [illegible]
002.07  ꝗ? ueni(?) / uim? [illegible]
002.08  ggaui? / gaudiꝰ? [illegible]  (begins with g-g; uncertain)
002.09  Dñi? / Drī? ꝗ? [h]ꝑpen? [illegible]  ("ꝑ" with a tall descender stroke)
002.10  Celebrar(e)? / Gelebrar? ꝗ? [illegible]
002.11  fuit? / punis? - hᵒ (hoc?) ꝗ? [illegible]  -ar? 
002.12  actas? / actus m[i]nores? / in core? [illegible]
002.13  [i]llius? obstat? ꝗ? [illegible]
002.14  Dici? / Dñi et officiu(m)? [illegible]
(Lines continue below into image-004/overlap.) Honest assessment: almost every word above is uncertain; only "offt", "dñi", "Si illis", "et" are moderately secure letter-shapes, and even those are not certain.

Right of crease (x 1095-1199), first letters only: nothing reliably legible ("ꝗ", "ri", "n" scattered).

TILE image-003.jpg (upper-right of face 1; native res). Overlaps image-002: x 0-140 here = x ~1060-1199 of image-002 (the line-beginnings column, right part). The straight vertical line at x ~150 here is a clean edge/crease running the full height; the text right of it (x 160-1160) has the same line pitch as the text left of it and the lines appear continuous across, so I treat it as one wide column crossed by a crease (still tentative -- it could be an overlapping repair strip). Right edge of text at x ~1160 = column end / leaf edge; holes at x 1035 y 450-560.
Larger letters at x ~940-1110, y ~580: "Qui lux"(?) -- written larger/bolder than the text hand, looks like the opening of a new unit (incipit or rubric-like; colour not determinable). 
Crops: crops/packet-06/i003_a.jpg (y 80-560), i003_b.jpg (y 540-1025), autocontrast x1.6.

Honest assessment: only "Qui lux", "in", "et", "sapie..." are reasonably visible as letter-shapes; "fonte/fonti", "filiꝫ", "laud-" are tentative. Most of this tile is effectively not read at word level -- the hand is small, cursive and abraded; higher resolution or UV would be needed.

TILE image-004.jpg (lower-left of face 1; native res). Overlaps image-002: 004 y 0-200 = 002 y ~830-1025 (line 004.01 "actas m.." = 002.12; 004.02 = 002.13; 004.03 = 002.14). Shows the left strip (line endings, x 40-300), the blank band with fold/strip join at x ~465 (holes at y 550, 790, 910), the column of line-beginnings (x 680-1060), crease at x ~1060, a few letters of the right part (x 1070-1199). Foot: modern pencil "Stams, STA, Frag. 34n"(?) at x 530-830, y 870-950. Lower margin c. 150 px below last line; lower edge torn on the left.
The column's last line (004.12) is followed by blank margin: so this is the foot of the column. "Per xpm" (004.11) is in a noticeably larger, bolder script at the line start -- display formula. The text hand is clearer here than in 002/003.
Crops: crops/packet-06/i004_col.jpg, i004_left.jpg (autocontrast x1.8).

004.01  actas? / ictus? m[i]nores? / in core? ... [illegible]       (= 002.12)

Honest assessment: "in flamma"/"flamma" (here and in the left strip 004.L09), "nulla", "magestas/maiestas", "celest-", "sapie-", "in honore Dei", "Per xpm", "xpm", "Qui lux" are my best-seen words; most others are letter-shape guesses. The vocabulary (xpm, celest-, maiestas, flamma, honore Dei, laud-) points to religious prose, but I make no identification.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-006, overview face 2 = the other side of the same piece; same size, mirrored outline -- the torn notch that was at left on face 1 is now at upper right)
- Left block (x ~715-955): a dense written block, c. 30+ lines, darker and more compressed than face 1; some lines look larger/bolder (possible headings or display lines around y 525, 580, 615); one reddish touch near x 715,y 555 (possible rubric/initial colour, uncertain at this scale).
- Vertical crease at x ~958 (same straight line as on face 1).
- Middle (x ~965-1060): a column of SHORT lines (single words / short phrases, e.g. "...sola", "...pena"), set narrower than the main block: looks like a narrow column, a list, or line-beginnings of a column whose remainder is lost/blank (tentative).
- Stained band x ~1060-1100, then right strip (x ~1100-1205) of text that looks like line-beginnings/full lines of another column on the far side of the fold.
- Modern pencil: "IX a/N 29" (rotated, x ~1040-1090, y 670-770) and "Stams, STA, Frag 34h"(?) at the foot -- not text.

TILE image-007.jpg (upper-left of face 2; native res). IMPORTANT LAYOUT OBSERVATION: the left block on this face carries two layers:
  (1) faint grey-brown small cursive-influenced Gothic text (the same kind of hand as face 1) -- this is the written text of this side;
  (2) a darker, browner, LARGER textualis script that is MIRROR-REVERSED (letter forms read backwards, e.g. reversed minim clusters and reversed d/b) -- an offset/transfer from another leaf (or strong show-through), lying between and over the grey lines. I have NOT transcribed the offset; it should not be taken as text of this leaf.
Small red touches at the left edge (x ~65,y 615; x ~100,y 905; x ~60,y 990) -- possibly rubricated paragraph marks/initial strokes (tentative). Crease at x ~1045; right of it (x 1050-1183) the beginning of the narrow middle column (only fragments of letters, mostly stained).

TILE image-008.jpg (upper-right of face 2; native res). Overlaps 007: x 0-115 here = x ~1065-1183 of 007; crease at x ~115 here.
